engine: Handlebars. Register helpers: pct(x) -> '12.6%', pct2(x) -> '12.63%', money(x, ccy) -> 'EUR 9.5M' (millions, 1dp) , num(x) -> thousands separators, date(iso) -> '29 Sep 2026', upper(s).
fill_order: 1. Build the context from the case (Neo4j) and the rule engine: every data field below.
2. Call the strong model ONCE with the system prompt below, the full data context, and the ai_slots list; it returns JSON {slot_name: markdown_text}.
3. Validate: every slot present, within max_words, no numbers that are not in the data context (reject and retry once).
4. Render the template with {...data, ai: slots}. Log the fill as an AuditEvent.
system_prompt: You are a senior transfer pricing consultant drafting sections of an OECD-style local file. You will receive (a) a JSON data context produced by a deterministic engine and approved by a consultant and (b) a list of narrative slots with instructions. Return ONLY a JSON object mapping each slot name to markdown text. Rules: use only facts and numbers present in the data context; never invent figures, dates, company names or legal references; quote percentages exactly as given; cite the reference string from the data when you state a legal requirement (e.g. '(OECD TPG Ch. III)'); where a reference contains 'verify', append '[to be verified]'; write in formal, audit-ready third person; if the data is insufficient for a statement, write '[Consultant to confirm: <what is missing>]' instead of guessing.

status.source: 'Draft' until all approvals exist, then 'Final draft for review'

entity.*.source: LegalEntity node / entities.csv row for the tested party

group.name / parent_name / parent_countr.example: Novatek Group / Novatek Holdings Inc. / United States

tested.transaction_summary.source: derived: largest controlled transaction(s) involving the tested party in FY
tested.transaction_summary.example: Purchase of finished sensors from Novatek Holdings Inc. for resale in EMEA (USD 198.2M)

transactions[].source: Transaction nodes where provider or recipient = tested party, FY = year

far.*.source: approved FARAssessment (approved_json) + audit event of approval

methods.{cup,rpm,cpm_cost_plus,tnmm,psm}.source: method selection step; defaults below until the method engine exists

cup: No reliable internal or external comparable uncontrolled prices for the same products and terms.
rpm: Gross margin data for independent distributors is not reliably comparable due to accounting differences in cost classification.
cpm_cost_plus: Gross mark-up data is not reliably comparable; net-level indicators are more robust.
tnmm: Tested party is the least complex party; reliable net margin data is available for independent comparables.
psm: Only one party makes unique and valuable contributions; the tested party performs routine functions.

fields: conclusion_label ('Outside the arm's length range' | 'Within the arm's length range')

executive_summary.instruction: Summarise the tested transaction, method, PLI, the tested party's weighted result versus the interquartile range, and the conclusion and adjustment. One paragraph.

scope_purpose.instruction: State the purpose of the document (local file for the entity and fiscal year) and what it covers.

thresholds_and_deadlines.instruction: Explain which documentation requirements apply to this entity based on the triggers (e.g. thresholds exceeded, new transactions). Cite each reference. Do not invent due dates.

entity_business_description.instruction: Describe what the entity does using role, key_functions and the approved FAR.

management_structure.instruction: Describe reporting lines to the parent as evidenced by the FAR (e.g. pricing and marketing decided by HQ). If unknown, use the consultant-to-confirm placeholder.

restructurings.instruction: Describe any new transactions or changes in the year (transactions whose first_year equals the fiscal year), especially intangibles. State 'None identified' if there are none.

group_overview.instruction: Describe the group's structure and each entity's role in one short paragraph.

industry_analysis.instruction: Describe the industry and market in which the entity operates. Use only information in the context (and retrieved sources, if provided with URLs). Otherwise write a neutral description flagged '[Consultant to confirm]'.

value_drivers.instruction: Identify the main value drivers (technology, brand, customer relationships, manufacturing) and which entity owns or controls each, per the FAR.

tested_transaction_description.instruction: Describe the tested transaction: parties, flow of goods or services, pricing mechanism, and amounts.

intercompany_agreements.instruction: State which transactions are covered by written agreements and which are not, and why missing agreements matter (cite the rule reference).

functions_narrative.instruction: Narrate the functions table: what the tested party does and what the parent controls.

assets_narrative.instruction: Describe tangible and intangible assets employed by the tested party versus the parent.

risks_narrative.instruction: Apply the six-step risk framework to the key risks, concluding which party controls and bears each.

characterisation.instruction: Conclude the entity's characterisation (e.g. limited-risk distributor) and the expected profile of returns.

method_selection.instruction: Explain why TNMM is the most appropriate method, referencing the methods table. Mention the US CPM equivalent.

tested_party_selection.instruction: Explain why this entity is the tested party (least complex, no unique intangibles).

pli_selection.instruction: Explain why the chosen PLI fits the entity's functions (operating margin for distributors; net cost plus for service providers).

search_strategy.instruction: Describe the search and screening approach and the independence and loss criteria. Note that the candidate set is illustrative.

range_interpretation.instruction: Explain the interquartile range and why the median is the adjustment point under this analysis.

results_comparison.instruction: Compare the tested party's weighted and current-year results with the range, and explain the drivers of any deviation using FAR flags and triggers (e.g. a new royalty).

conclusion.instruction: State the arm's length conclusion and the recommended adjustment. Do not introduce new numbers.

recommendations.instruction: Turn the triggers into prioritised, concrete actions (e.g. draft the licence agreement, year-end true-up), each with its reference.

assumptions_limitations.instruction: List assumptions and limitations: illustrative data and thresholds, AI-assisted drafting with consultant approval, and items marked for confirmation.
